claims.statement: For a fixed eligible pair and its contract selector, injectivity of the mark-preserving map d_p:M_p(H_v,W_v)->M_{p-1}(H_v,W_v) for every selected original leaf implies S(T,p)<=0.
claims.scope: Conditional criterion for the exact residuals H_v=T-{v,s_v}, W_v=N_T(s_v)\{v}, p-1 rank, and fixed F(T,p); no injectivity premise is proved for general eligible trees.
claims.reason: retained: finite-dimensional injectivity gives q_p<=q_{p-1} for each selected leaf, and the contract summand equals q_p-q_{p-1}. The 19-vertex Boolean example only obstructs an unselected rank and proves no target counterexample.

claims.statement: For every eligible lower-region pair (T,p) with T=K_{1,m}, m>=4, every original leaf is selected and S(T,p)=m*(binom(m-1,p)-binom(m-1,p-1))<0.
claims.scope: Ordinary stars only, under x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, with alpha(T)=m and each original leaf counted separately.
claims.reason: retained: exact zero-extended counts establish x=floor((m-1)/2)+1; deleting any leaf gives K_{1,m-1} with Delta_p<0 throughout the eligible rank range; the complete sum is the stated negative binomial difference times m.

limitations: The star subcase does not prove the aggregate for arbitrary ordinary trees.
The operator criterion remains conditional; no general residual injectivity or aggregate rank inequality was established.
The dimension obstruction is outside the selector-eligible range and is not a counterexample.
The arithmetic replay covered the two supplied m=20 examples and the stated dimension example, while the universal star formulas were checked symbolically.
